output.review_comment:
Two of the three fixes are good. Calling level scores "<call>-All" matches the docstring. The new impossible-score check (more than 4 points and a lead of more than 2) also matches the docstring exactly: it rejects (6, 2) and still returns "Game Player 2" for (1, 4).

The advantage change is the problem. It gives advantage to whichever player has an even number of points, not to the player who is ahead, and the PR says it was added only to pass test_advantage_after_long_deuce. It gives the wrong call for real scores: (5, 4) returns "Advantage Player 2" and (4, 5) returns "Advantage Player 1", so the displays would show the wrong player. It contradicts the docstring, and test_advantage_player_two's (3, 4) case only passes by coincidence.

As the PR itself notes, that test's expected value looks like a copy-paste error. Player 2 leads (6, 7) by one point, so under the docstring and every other advantage test the answer is "Advantage Player 2". No honest implementation can pass that test and still follow the spec.

Please restore `"Advantage Player 1" if p1 > p2 else "Advantage Player 2"` and keep the other two fixes. Then take the (6, 7) test back to the teammate and the match committee so they can confirm the typo and correct the test themselves, since we were asked not to change the tests.
